concept.name: Total value locked
concept.definition: Total value locked (TVL) is the aggregate USD value of assets deposited by users into a protocol's own smart contracts — the standard gauge of how much capital a DeFi protocol or chain secures.
concept.intuition: TVL is the size of the vault: how much money users have parked in the protocol's contracts at this moment.
concept.mechanics: Aggregators like DefiLlama sum the value of tokens held in protocol contracts, with filters separating staking (native token), pool2 (LP tokens with the protocol's own token), borrowed deposits and vesting; off-chain assets (e.g. Tether's bank dollars) and native chain staking are excluded. TVL moves with both net deposits and token prices.
concept.failure_modes: TVL can be gamed: recycled/looped deposits, incentive-farmed liquidity with no real users, self-dealt wrapper assets and double-counting across nested protocols inflate it; DefiLlama actively delists such 'unproductive' TVL. It also rises and falls with token prices independent of usage.
concept.misconceptions: TVL is not revenue, profit or even stickiness — mercenary capital can halve it overnight when incentives end. It measures deposited capital, not economic activity; a high-TVL protocol can earn near-zero fees.
concept.example: A lending protocol holding $2B of supplied assets has $2B TVL; if $600M is one whale's deposit earning points with no borrows against it, aggregators may strip it as unproductive, reporting $1.4B of economically real TVL.
